name: ANSI/IEEE conductor junction symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented junction dot marking a connection between crossing or meeting conductors on an ANSI-style schematic.
description: In ANSI-style schematics a solid dot at the meeting of conductors indicates an electrical connection. Unlike some IEC practice, readers in this convention often treat any crossing without a dot as not connected and expect a dot even on tees, so the dot carries more weight than it does on IEC drawings.

This is a convention-specific lookup. The geometry here is independently drawn to explain the connection; it is not a certified reproduction of the IEEE graphic. The dot only states continuity; the physical joint may be a terminal, lug or splice elsewhere.
readingNotes: Read any undotted crossing as unconnected unless the legend says otherwise.
Confirm the physical connection point on the wiring diagram.
drawingChecklist: Place a dot at every intended connection.
Avoid dots on crossings that are not connected.
Keep the dot size legible after reduction.
distinction: The junction dot shows connection; the ANSI crossing hop shows deliberately unconnected conductors.
